query: What signals suggest an incident resolution will be inefficient?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Resolution time is the primary basis on which 'inefficient resolution' is defined; it is only known once the incident is closed (post-outcome) and is effectively the outcome itself, so it leaks the focus rather than predicting it.

per_column.name: hours_to_last_update
per_column.rationale: Measured from open to the last update, this is a post-hoc duration highly collinear with total resolution time (identical value distribution here), knowable only after the incident progresses; it restates/leaks the inefficiency signal.

per_column.name: assignee_changed
per_column.rationale: Reassignment (ping-ponging) is an antecedent process characteristic that plausibly precedes and predicts inefficient handling without being a deterministic function of the outcome definition; a legitimate predictor, though it can partly reflect an already-troubled ticket.

per_column.name: is_high_priority
per_column.rationale: Priority is set at/near intake, lies outside the resolution-efficiency outcome, and plausibly carries predictive signal about handling effort and resolution efficiency.

per_column.name: inefficiency_score
per_column.rationale: A composite named directly after inefficiency is a derived restatement/label of the focus construct (likely built from resolution_hours and reassignment), not an independent external predictor; it circularly encodes the target.

judge.rationale: Three of five columns (resolution_hours, hours_to_last_update, inefficiency_score) either leak or restate the outcome that defines inefficient resolution and would be unavailable before the outcome or circularly derived from it. Only assignee_changed and is_high_priority are genuine ex-ante predictors external to the focus, giving modest but real predictive leverage beyond the original schema.
